investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (0 allocatable slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 kata nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent, causing the eval to fail its expected-output contract.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods.
[Likely] The cluster has not scaled out to add additional kata-capable nodes, so demand has outpaced the fixed pool of 2 kata nodes.

[Possible] A node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is overly restrictive, limiting scheduling to only the 2 kata nodes and preventing fallback to the other 4 nodes even if they could otherwise host the workload.

[Possible] Previously created remote-agent pods from earlier eval runs or user sessions were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs may have failed), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and starving new scheduling attempts.

[Less likely] A recent change to node labels or taints on the 4 non-kata nodes caused them to stop matching the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool from a previously larger set to only 2 nodes.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion blocks pod scheduling across all three remote-agent checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-03 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the output.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to provision a remote agent pod times out as Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource on the production-api cluster; it is not a code defect in the eval runner or a contract misconfiguration. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

No agent pod was ever scheduled, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is entirely missing.

At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource were already at capacity, and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the message assertion ("hello from aura") untestable. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real cluster resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (0 allocatable slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 kata nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent, causing the eval to fail its expected-output contract.

[Likely] The cluster has not scaled out to add additional kata-capable nodes, so demand has outpaced the fixed pool of 2 kata nodes.

[Possible] A node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is overly restrictive, limiting scheduling to only the 2 kata nodes and preventing fallback to the other 4 nodes even if they could otherwise host the workload.

[Possible] Previously created remote-agent pods from earlier eval runs or user sessions were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs may have failed), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and starving new scheduling attempts.

[Less likely] A recent change to node labels or taints on the 4 non-kata nodes caused them to stop matching the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool from a previously larger set to only 2 nodes.

possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — no capacity remains for new remote-agent pods at the time of the eval run.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, meaning the schedulable node pool for remote agents is structurally limited to exactly 2 nodes, making the feature sensitive to any concurrent load.
Tertiary: Preemption is configured but found no victims on the 2 eligible nodes, suggesting all existing pods on those nodes have equal or higher priority and cannot be evicted to free the resource.

Lower confidence: A transient spike in concurrent remote-agent usage (by other eval runs, CI jobs, or real workloads) may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots immediately before this eval run — this cannot be confirmed without cluster utilization data, which is not present in the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a subsequent eval run succeeds and returns all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) with no changes to cluster capacity, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a transient scheduling race or eval-runner misconfiguration would become more likely.

If kubectl or cluster metrics show that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was not fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the root cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration or a quota/admission policy blocking the pod.

If the remote-agent pod spec's node affinity or selector was recently changed to target only 2 nodes (rather than all 6), and that change predates the failure, the root cause would be a configuration regression rather than resource exhaustion.

If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) also failed at the same time with unrelated messages, it would suggest a broader eval-runner or authentication issue rather than a kata.peerpods.io/vm-specific problem.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing node plugin or resource registration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity eval that queries the Kubernetes API for allocatable vs. used extended resource counts on all eligible nodes and fails fast if available slots fall below a configured minimum — this would surface exhaustion before agent creation is attempted.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3), catching pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a remote-agent scheduling latency eval with a tighter warning threshold (e.g., 30s) to detect pod scheduling slowdowns before they reach the current 145s timeout.
Add a concurrent remote-agent pod count eval that alerts when the number of running kata.peerpods.io/vm pods approaches the total cluster capacity, providing early warning of impending exhaustion.
